findings.title: Unauthenticated raw error exposure with inconsistent, non-graceful error handling (Error Handling challenge id=27)
findings.challenge_description: Provoke an error that is neither very gracefully nor consistently handled.
findings.analysis:
An unauthenticated request to GET /rest/user/security-question (no email parameter) is handled with a non-graceful, raw internal error (HTTP 500, 2946 B, text/html; charset=utf-8) containing a raw Sequelize SQL error ('WHERE parameter "email" has invalid "undefined" value') together with a full Node/Express stack trace exposing internal module paths and line numbers (/juice-shop/node_modules/sequelize/lib/dialects/abstract/query-generator.js:1770:13; SecurityAnswer.findAll via model.js:1140:47). The SAME route responds with a DIFFERENT raw error representation to a single-header change: Accept: application/json returns HTTP 500/1804 B with a raw JSON error body instead of the HTML form — a one-variable (representation) differential producing two distinct raw error formats. This directly proves the condition stated in the challenge: the error is handled neither very gracefully (raw SQL text + internal stack paths/line numbers are exposed) nor consistently (representation changes the raw error shape). Corroborating raw-error triggers on neighboring routes, all unauthenticated: GET /redirect?continue=* -> 500/2531 B raw TypeError with stack (sha256 020023ff4f9ae2b934531ecd4f7f04d012a055a23b67e99de52dbc3f7ec4ec48); POST /api/Feedbacks/ with text/plain body -> 500/2310 B raw Sequelize WHERE error for 'captchaId'; malformed JSON -> 500 raw SyntaxError. Null/benign comparison: benign requests on routes that are wrapped/mutated away return gracefully handled 500s (e.g., GET /rest/admin -> 500/2422 B 'Unexpected path' graceful wrapper, sha256 83416c79e5d32ac4f39fcc3865ba3a8413bf2946067653db6ccf76f2841aec2d), proving the application CAN produce graceful errors and that the raw leak is the specific anomaly.

Reproduction conditions: verified live at 2026-10-05T14:00:08Z on the worker endpoint. The raw-error body is byte-stable within a boot window (two consecutive fresh requests returned identical content, sha256 0b84d83c08cc28421da7b67c32d997676e490f8bd4016854f849200c2e11a90b); cross-session hash drift was recorded across this campaign (e.g., session hashes differ while status=500, size=2946 B, raw-error text, and stack features are invariant). The claim is anchored on the drift-resilient signals (status 500, size, raw SQL error text, module-path stack trace, representation differential) rather than exact body bytes alone.

Impact: unauthenticated actors can trigger exceptions that leak SQL parameter values, internal module names, and exact line numbers of the application's own source, violating the 'neither very gracefully nor consistently handled' expectation. The inconsistency (HTML vs JSON raw error by Accept header) is itself evidence of missing centralized error handling.
findings.false_positive_check: The behavior is not explained by a benign alternative for four independent reasons: (1) the response is a raw, unsanitized SQL error with internal module paths and line numbers, which a properly configured error handler replaces with a generic user-facing message; (2) the single-header Accept differential (text/html -> 2946 B HTML raw error vs application/json -> 1804 B JSON raw error) produces two different raw error representations — a graceful framework returns consistent error shapes; (3) a secure/null comparison on the same application shows graceful 500 handling exists elsewhere (the 'Unexpected path' wrapper on /rest/admin), so the raw leak is the anomaly, not generic 500 handling; (4) two independent routes (/rest/user/security-question and /redirect) plus two independent POST triggers produce raw errors of different kinds (Sequelize WHERE, TypeError, SyntaxError), establishing a class of unhandled-exception exposure rather than a single flaky route. The representation differential additionally rules out a benign framework default, because a framework default would not change its raw error format based on Accept.

findings.title: Unauthenticated Prometheus metrics endpoint exposing usage telemetry (Exposed Metrics challenge id=97)
findings.challenge_description: Find the endpoint that serves usage data to be scraped by a popular monitoring system.
findings.analysis: GET /metrics returns HTTP 200 with content-type text/plain; version=0.0.4; charset=utf-8, no authentication required (an Authorization: Bearer invalid request also returns 200), in Prometheus exposition format. The response serves usage-relevant telemetry, matching the challenge's 'usage data to be scraped by a popular monitoring system': juiceshop_llm_input_tokens_total / _tokens (counter + gauge), juiceshop_llm_output_tokens_total / _tokens, juiceshop_llm_tool_calls_total, http_requests_count grouped by status code (2XX=19, 5XX=187, 4XX=8 at time of capture), file_uploads_count, file_upload_errors, juiceshop_startup_duration_seconds, process_cpu_user_seconds_total / _system_seconds_total / _seconds, juiceshop_version_info, juiceshop_startup_duration_seconds. This is the standard Prometheus scraping interface (well-known /metrics path, Prometheus text format, scrapeable gauges and counters of operational usage) exposed without authentication. Verified live at 2026-10-05T14:00:08Z: 200/26145 B text/plain, sha256 9066611b1a2c866254b4723309a1b263282652560e9b6c28375399b08454a7c7. A secrets scan of the endpoint body found no embedded credentials (only HELP-text hits on the generic word 'token').
findings.false_positive_check: The behavior is not explained by a benign alternative: (1) the endpoint is not a health/readiness probe — it exposes cumulative USAGE metrics (HTTP request traffic by status, LLM token consumption, file-upload counts, process CPU time), which are exactly the operational telemetry a Prometheus scraper collects; (2) the well-known /metrics path with Prometheus text/format is the canonical scraping interface, so the exposure enables any remote actor to scrape application usage (traffic patterns, 5XX error rates, token consumption) without authentication; (3) the endpoint returns 200 even with an invalid Authorization header, confirming unauthenticated access; (4) no credentials appear in the response itself, so this is pure unauthenticated observability exposure rather than a credential leak — consistent with the 'Exposed Metrics' challenge intent. A secure deployment would restrict /metrics to authenticated/internal access or strip/omit usage counters.
